title: Localized SLO decomposition and notify-gating proposal
summary: Draft proposal for splitting global SLOs into localized component SLOs and gating pager notifications with lightweight correlation rules to reduce noisy SLO-burn pages while preserving true incident visibility.
content:
Context and motivation:

- We continue to get a significant fraction of paging noise from global SLO burn alerts that originate from a narrow class of dependency regressions (eg: instrumenter exporters, k/v cache metric drops, and downstream telemetry stalls). These pages often wake the on-call but do not require service-level mitigations (often operator actions at the telemetry layer).
- Our current approach: single global SLOs per product surface (api-latency-slo, generation-success-slo) and immediate pager for burn > 2% sustained over 5m. This is easy to reason about but amplifies noisy upstream signals.

Goals for this proposal:

1) Reduce pager volume by only paging when the SLO burn indicates a probable customer impact vs telemetry-only failures.
2) Improve signal locality so engineers can take fast, scoped actions rather than broad rollbacks.
3) Keep overall error budget accounting unchanged (we still measure global SLOs) but decompose ownership for faster remediation and less interruption.

High-level idea:

- Decompose selected global SLOs into localized component SLOs that represent the health of critical internal subsystems and their contribution to the global SLO. Example component SLOs: kvcache-hit-stability, prefix-cache-kv-exporter-availability, request-serializer-success-rate, region-egress-latency.
- Add a notify-gating layer for pager rules: an SLO-burn alert will escalate to page only when the global SLO burn is accompanied by either (A) at least one component SLO breaching AND a customer-facing metric (p50/p95 latency or error rate) crossing a preconfigured threshold, or (B) multiple component SLOs in the same failure domain breaching simultaneously.
- If only a single telemetry/exporter component SLO is degraded while customer-facing metrics remain within tolerance, route the alert to a lower-severity channel (team slack, ops queue) with automated diagnostic captures and suggested remediation playbooks.

Why this is different from simple suppression:

- We are not muting alerts; we are adding a correlation layer that aims to match alerts to probable customer impact. The global SLO measurement and burn remain unchanged for reporting and product decisions. The gating only affects the paging lifecycle and human routing.

Practical decomposition (initial rollout candidates):

- Hosted API global latency SLO -> decompose into: regional-inference-latency, kvcache-latency-contribution, exporter-metrics-availability, autoscaler-throttle-events.
- Embeddings ingestion success SLO -> decompose into: batch-queue-accept-rate, model-serve-availability, storage-writes-success-rate.

Heuristics for gating rules (first-pass):

- Gate A (customer-impact required): Page if global SLO burn > 2% for 5m AND (p95 latency increase > 30% OR user-facing error-rate increase > 1% absolute) AND any component SLO breach.
- Gate B (multi-component burst): Page if > 2 component SLOs in same domain (eg: telemetry exporters) breach within 3m window regardless of immediate customer metric change. Rationale: multi-component failures often indicate systemic regressions requiring broader action.
- Lower tier routing: If only a single telemetry/exporter component SLO breaches but customer metrics stable, create an Ops ticket and post in #sre-ops with attached diagnostic snapshot, suggested quick checks, and a 30m auto-escalation timer if the component SLO does not recover or customer metrics degrade.

Required telemetry and dashboards:

- New component SLO dashboards (per subsystem): time-series, burn heatmap, correlated traces, top-10 affected request routes.
- A correlation engine dashboard showing active gates, which gate triggered, and the diagnostic snapshot used to make routing decisions.
- Automated diagnostic snapshots to include: last 10 exporter logs, recent histogram of prefix lengths, kv-cache hit/miss rates, top 5 host latencies.

Experiment plan (6 weeks):

Week 0-1: Instrumentation
- Define and implement component SLOs as derived metrics (avoid adding new instrumentation where possible; use existing exporter metrics and labels).
- Add ephemeral dashboards and alert rules in the test (staging) environment.

Week 2: Canary routing
- Deploy gating logic for a subset of services (one product line: hosted-api region-us-west) in monitor-only mode (no pages, just logs of what would have paged). Collect sample for 7 days.

Week 3-4: Review and tune
- Review false negatives/positives from canary. Refine thresholds and which components count as customer-impacting. Prioritize simplicity: prefer a few well-understood components over many brittle signals.

Week 5: Gradual rollout
- Enable lower-tier routing for all regions and enable paging for Gate A/B where canary behaved as expected. Maintain quick rollback path (toggle per-product gating in config).

Week 6: Post-rollout evaluation
- Compare page counts, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to restore (MTTR) for affected SLOs vs baseline. Evaluate error budget accounting for global SLO and confirm no silent burn leakage.

On-call playbook (for gated alerts routed to ops queue):

1) Read automated diagnostic snapshot attached. Look for immediate indicators: exporter crash, 5xx spike on ingress, throttling events.
2) Run the three quick checks: (a) exporter process status on collectors, (b) recent prometheus scrape success rate for the exporter, (c) check k/v cache eviction lag.
3) If the snapshot shows telemetry-only issues (exporter errors, scrape failure), follow the telemetry restart checklist attached (restart exporter, validate scrape, confirm metrics flow). Mark ticket with steps taken.
4) If customer-facing metrics degrade while gate suppressed paging, escalate immediately to primary on-call and disable gating for that SLO until root cause is found.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Gate rules might introduce false negatives that suppress pages for real customer impact.
  Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, canary mode, and automatic escalation if any customer-facing metric worsens even after gating.

- Risk: Increased complexity makes SLO ownership blurry.
  Mitigation: clear owner mapping per component SLO and a simple runbook that lists who to call for each component failure.

- Risk: Diagnostic snapshot generation adds load to monitoring pipelines.
  Mitigation: sample-based generation (only for alerts) and capped snapshot size.

Open questions (to resolve during design phase):

- Which specific component SLOs should be first-class (we want to avoid proliferation)? Proposal: start with telemetry/exporter availability, kvcache hit-stability, model-serving-availability, and autoscaler-throttle-rate.
- How to encode domain grouping (eg telemetry layer vs compute vs network) robustly in our metrics? Tagging conventions and stricter label hygiene will be required.
- How to present gating state to on-call in the console (clear UI affordance needed so paging status is obvious)?

Next actions (owners):

- Aisha: draft component SLO definitions and labels (due 2025-02-17).
- Marco: prototype a correlation rule in staging and run monitor-only sample collection (due 2025-02-24).
- Jin: design diagnostic snapshot schema and storage limits (due 2025-02-21).
- Ellen: prepare communication plan and SRE training doc for new gating behavior (due 2025-02-28).

Notes to reviewers:

- This is a safety-first proposal: if in doubt we page. The intention is to reduce fatigue from noisy telemetry-only pages and route low-impact work to an ops queue with helpful automated context.
- Please annotate the component SLO suggestions with concrete metric names when commenting (eg apply prometheus metric name and label set).

Appendix: example alert flow (short):

1) Global SLO burn triggers an evaluation rule.
2) Correlation engine queries component SLOs and customer metrics (p95/p50/5xx).
3) If Gate A or Gate B matches -> escalate to pager. Else -> create ops ticket + post snapshot to #sre-ops.

Observability TODOs (technical):

- Add prometheus derived rules for component SLOs (ex: kvcache_hit_stability = 1 - rate(kvcache_miss_total[5m]) with target 0.98).
- Add a small lambda service (or extend current alertmanager webhook) that implements the gating decisions and can be toggled per-namespace.
- Add labels to scraped metrics to identify domain (domain=telemetry|compute|network|storage).

End.
